verdict.rationale: Google Cloud documents fine-grained IAM ('who can do what on which resource') and Workload Identity Federation, which gives workloads access through federated identities instead of long-lived service account keys. Together these are building blocks for scoped, keyless credentials. The evidence does not show any agent-specific pattern, nor explicit temporary or time-bound credentials or anti-escalation guarantees. Missing for 10: documented agent-specific credential patterns, explicit short-lived/time-bound token issuance, controls preventing privilege escalation, independent or hands-on corroboration.
